So I write as a hobby, usually just stuff for myself or occasionally for writing subs elsewhere on the internet, I find it relaxing. Lately I have been wondering what it would be like if fat was seen as the vile, rotten disease of lazy inhumans that it is. What would happen if some kind of institution were to dedicate itself to getting rid of fat at any and all costs, treating the fats as the sub-humans that they are until they are able to reach a human size again. What kind of punishment they would get for not cooperating, what techniques they would be subjected to for weight loss.

Going for a dark mood, with the possibility of taking on a horror genre in time for Halloween, how many of these techniques would be seen as torturous and what sort of behaviours from the fat people would demonstrate the selfish inhumanness that poses extreme risks to the humans around them?

For example, I wrote a conversation between two people describing an event in which a fat person was in an extreme weight loss facility, threw a tantrum, and in its rage pushed the nurse escorting it to its room down a flight of stairs, only to lose its balance and fall down after, resulting in the nurse's death. There are hundreds of real life stories in which fat people have murdered by falling on top of others, smothering and suffocating them, so having real stories to work off of makes the danger more real in the story.

But I need more inspiration. I see at least five posts every day here about someone's rage-inducing experience with a fatty, and I want to hear what you would do to, if you could do anything at all, to force the fatty that haunts your life to lose weight. What would you say to it, how would you treat it? What do you wish you could force it to understand about itself? How would you punish it for not cooperating with the weight loss plan?

It can be as dark or as innocent as you like, but tell me in as many or few words as you like, what would your perfect fat camp be like?

Or, what are some of the most horrifying things you have heard a ham do to someone, or seen a ham go through itself? Anything from sitting on a child to developing a yeast infection so bad it causes a stroke in the ham itself.

Hams are walking piles of danger and disaster, for themselves and for everyone around them. I want this story to emulate all our worst fears and experiences of this fact.

So go on, my friends, inspire me, make me shudder in horror, make me sick to my stomach.

I will not copy your stories for mine, and will only take some creative cues inspired by what I see here.

That's not good enough. A person chooses to walk armed or not. Even in a gun free zone I have a few ways of legally equipping myself.

This didn't happen in a vacuum. There are always weapons around.

Now would be the time for an entrepreneur martial artist to create a style around the tools at the ready disposal that can easily be used for a weapon, and train their brethren in how to fight. What people don't understand about the context of older martial arts like karate, styles that used tools like sais, nunchuks, a staff, etc. is that those were common farming tools that wouldn't look out of place for people to walk around with. They were the only way that the common people could defend themselves against the warrior class above them with their swords.

I think that's what's lacking from the modern day in a lot of ways. There is a solid argument for practicing and honoring the older styles while keeping them in their original styles, and there are also solid arguments for modernizing them. Even though, some of the best weapon fighters are still limiting themselves to the ways of old. While I love what the Dog Brothers got going on in California, and I totally respect that, it's not quite the evolution I'm waiting for. I also like what they got going on in with the M1 guys got going on with their tournaments, I like that these types of things are coming along... and the UWM is paradoxically a fantastic step forward and backward. I think if people did it full time in practice, to do their full contact stuff, they won't learn to respect pain/fear quite as much as they should. I love that these types of fighting styles are coming into the mainstream a bit more overall.

The thing that is lacking to me, is that we haven't seen a new, modern style emerge yet. Unorthodox weapons training is just not practiced as much as it should be, from any school really, and it's a waste because it helps perpetuate this illusion that people aren't constantly surrounded by weapons at every moment. There are a few styles that can be used well for a cane, for older folks especially, Canne-de-combat, Kali/Eskrima to name off a couple that can be converted well for a weapon that is easy and convenient to carry around... but unless you're a pimp, young guys, it's weird if you carry a cane around. The point to a good martial artist is deception. Knives are great--there are tons of styles that practice with a knife because nearly every culture figured out how to make one and fight with them and do that well enough to build a system around it. One can be clever enough to realize that carrying around an unopened coke/beer bottle is far from suspicious to carry around, and if it's unopened their skull will break before the glass, and convert their knife training accordingly. I think if one was clever, you could build a style around fighting with a backpack. The point of the styles of old was converting casual, everyday items into weapons. There should be an evolution at some point to account for the modern day items of today built into a system and taught.

Even if you don't have a weapon, you always have your fists, feet, elbows, knees, you can wrestle, you can bite, you can head butt, you can fish hook, you can eye gouge--you have lots of options if you don't have a weapon easily accessible. If you have that difficult of a time having guns--then it should be assumed their opponent is having an equally difficult time and act accordingly.
